title: Longest unbroken ticket run
prompt:
Raffle tickets arrive in no particular order; return the length of the longest run of integers x, x+1, ..., x+m-1 that are all present among the tickets.

- tickets has 0 to 100,000 integers between -10^9 and 10^9, possibly with duplicates (a duplicate does not lengthen a run).
- Return 0 for an empty list.
- Aim for O(n) expected time: do not sort.
hints: Sorting solves it in O(n log n). With a set you can ask 'is x present?' in O(1).
Every run has exactly one starting value: the x for which x - 1 is missing.
Put all values in a set. For each value x with x - 1 not in the set, count upward while x + length is in the set and keep the maximum.

solution.explanation: Only values whose predecessor is absent start a run, so the inner counting loop runs only from run starts. Each value is visited by at most one such inner loop, so the total work is linear in the number of distinct values.

complexity.notes: Expected time with hashing. The nested loop is still linear because each value is counted from exactly one run start.

followUps: Return the run itself as [start, end] instead of its length, breaking ties by the smaller start.
How would you solve it with union-find, and when might that be preferable?
